subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode fix, should OpenClaw accept the native `@microsoft/mxc-sdk`/`node-pty` dependency graph and MXC SDK argv-carried base64 config boundary for this official Windows sandbox plugin?
rationale: The remaining code defect is mechanical, but accepting a native dependency with install scripts and a preview SDK transport for sandbox config is a security/ownership choice automation should not decide.

options.title: Fix guard, then approve exact-head dependencies
options.body: Add the full-mode registration guard and test, then merge only after admin/secops explicitly approves the dependency graph and argv boundary on the final head.

options.title: Pause for upstream transport
options.body: Keep the PR open or paused until MXC SDK provides a non-argv config transport or maintainers decide the preview boundary is acceptable.

options.title: Reject first-party MXC for now
options.body: Close or defer this first-party plugin direction if the native SDK and sandbox boundary are not acceptable for OpenClaw-owned distribution.

recommendation.title: Fix guard, then approve exact-head dependencies
recommendation.body: Add the full-mode registration guard and test, then merge only after admin/secops explicitly approves the dependency graph and argv boundary on the final head.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the latest concrete MXC/OpenShell parity and dependency-boundary review guidance on this PR.
